evals.name: arxiv-search-attention-mechanisms
evals.prompt: Research: I need to understand the current state of attention mechanisms for transformers — in particular, what alternatives to scaled dot-product attention have been proposed in the last 2 years that reduce quadratic complexity. I'm building a document processing pipeline and need to know whether to implement linear attention, sparse attention, or stick with standard attention plus chunking. Search arXiv and give me a primary-source brief.

assertions.text: Restates the topic as a research question before searching
Uses at least 3 keyword variants in the arXiv search (e.g. linear attention, sparse attention, efficient transformer)
Collects at least 5 candidate papers before filtering
Output follows the synthesis structure: Question, Papers, Findings, Recommendation, Risks, Practical notes
Each claim is backed by a specific paper with title, authors, and arXiv link
Practical notes include concrete implementation implications for the user's document processing pipeline

evals.name: inconclusive-research-handling
evals.prompt: Research: I need papers about using ferrofluid dynamics for database indexing in OLAP workloads. I heard someone mention this at a meetup. Search arXiv and tell me what you find.

assertions.text: Attempts the arXiv search despite the niche topic — does not refuse
Tries at least 3 keyword variants (e.g. ferrofluid database, magnetic indexing, unconventional data structures)
Plainly states the research is inconclusive if no relevant papers are found
Does not pad the brief with loosely related or irrelevant papers just to fill space
Recommends the next best query, experiment, or broader source (e.g. conference proceedings, project repos)
Appends a one-line entry to .research-log with topic, date, and key finding
